target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: lanceolate PATO_0001877 to obovate PATO_0001936)
reason: A shape between two existing values, like 'linear-lanceolate'. It is covered by the continuum pattern between two comparable values, not by a new term.
Half-ring-shaped (a disc or thickening reaching halfway round). PATO's semicircular, 'shape of half a circle', is the closest term. It is too rare to justify a half-ring class.
Nodose = knobbled under rule C331, so 'not nodose' is its negation, the same way 'unlobed' is not lobed.
This states that a neck is absent, but there is no PO or FLOPO neck class, and the previous review rejected 'neck' as a generic part.

label: oily
definition: A composition quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's containing an abundance of oil, as in oil-rich seeds, arils and endosperm. NOTE: Not PATO:0002114 fatty, which is an excess of lipid (a pathology), nor PATO:0001606 greasy, a coating.
reason: A standard description of seeds and arils with no PATO term. 'Fatty' carries the meaning of a pathological excess.

A compound of two values. The reversed form 'depressed-globose' was ruled oblate (C170), but 'globuleux-déprimé' reads as globose tending to depressed, so it goes to the continuum pattern. Oblate is the alternative reading.
PATO sparse is defined as 'scattered; spread irregularly, and at a distance from each other', which is exactly this wording for sori, glands and branches.

label: multilateral
definition: A positional quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of its flowers or branches being borne on all sides of the axis. NOTE: Opposite of FLOPO:0991146 secund and of PATO:0000634 unilateral.
reason: A real description of inflorescences, the opposite of secund/unilateral, with no existing term.
PATO sloped means 'having an oblique or slanted direction', which covers sloping shoulders, sepals and boles.

label: strangling
definition: A positional quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its beginning growth on a host tree and sending roots to the ground that enclose the host's trunk, often eventually killing it. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991110 epiphytic and FLOPO:0991108 climbing; probably outside PATO's scope (habit).
reason: A distinct, well-defined habit (strangler figs, Clusia) handled like the other habit values already in FLOPO.
Same as the existing rule for 'staminate' (C233): a flower that works only as male. 'Functionally' only notes that the female parts are rudimentary.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (region of the bearer): plant organ base (FLOPO_0985024) + increased thickness (PATO_0000591)
reason: The quality belongs to the base of the part, not the whole part, so it is a part-of-the-bearer annotation using existing terms.
A figurative word whose meaning changes with the bearer (bark pattern, roots wrapped round a bulb, twisted awns). It has no single quality.

target: new: conjunction of two values (papillose FLOPO:0991059 and serrulate FLOPO:0991081)
reason: A margin that is finely toothed by projecting papillae, so both values hold at once. This is a compound to annotate with both terms, not a new class.

target: new: coloured marking (spotted PATO_0000333 with the marks purple PATO_0000951)
reason: Flecked = spotted (rule C335), plus the colour of the flecks. This needs a pattern linking the marking to its colour, not a colour-specific term.
Sparsely pilose. The quality is pilose and 'scattered' is a density modifier kept in the record, not a separate term.
Tongue-like (lingulate) is the same flat, elongate, rounded-tipped shape as ligulate, which was ruled strap-shaped (C189).

label: vermiform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being worm-shaped: long, narrow, cylindrical and usually curved or twisted. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0002430 strap-shaped, which is flat.
reason: A standard shape term for propagules, sclereids and scales with no PATO equivalent. Used rarely, but it has one clear meaning.
An inflorescence that resembles an umbel without being a true umbel, which is exactly the definition of umbelliform.

target: prickle (PO_0025169) or thorn (PO_0025172) or spine leaf (PO_0025173) present
reason: 'Armed' means bearing prickles, thorns or spines, i.e. one of these parts is present (a union). 'Sparsely' is a frequency modifier kept in the record.
Pinniveined is a synonym of pinnately veined.
Raised veins stand out from the surface. PATO raised (PATO_0001369) is about microbial colonies; prominent ('projecting beyond a surface') is the right term, and 'slightly' is a degree modifier.
Canoe-shaped = boat-shaped, ruled scaphoid (C213).
A fruit or stem 'with a bloom' has a waxy, rub-off coating, which is the PATO definition of glaucous (same as the pruinose rule C222).

target: new: conjunction of two values (obtuse PATO_0001935 with mucronate FLOPO:0991054)
reason: A blunt apex ending in a small point: two values that both hold. PATO lists 'apiculate' only as a synonym of the attribute 'sharpness', which should not be used as a value.
A thin, hard, brittle crust, as in a crustose pericarp, seed coat or holdfast. This is the crustaceous value.

target: new: conjunction of two values (glandular PATO_0002117 and foveate PATO_0002296)
reason: A fruit surface pitted with glands, so both values hold. Annotate with both existing terms rather than a compound term.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum: obovate PATO_0001936 to oblong PATO_0000946)
reason: A shape between two values plus a width modifier. Covered by the continuum pattern.
A position stated relative to another part, recorded with 'towards' the sepals.

'Déhiscents' and 'dehiscence along a suture' state that the part opens, which is the dehiscent value. Where the way of opening is given, the more specific value (e.g. circumscissile for 'transversale') applies.
